description: Normative global 1.5°C pathway reaching net zero CO2 around 2050; REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3.
pathwayDescription:
The Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS) develops reference climate transition and physical risk scenarios to support financial institutions, regulators, and policymakers in assessing climate-related financial risks. These scenarios provide globally consistent projections of emissions, energy systems, and macroeconomic trends under varying policy and temperature pathways. Their Net Zero 2050, REMIND-MAgPIE 3.3-4.8 (NZ2050 REMIND) Scenario is a normative, high-ambition global pathway in which the world achieves net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050, consistent with limiting warming to below 1.5°C. It assumes immediate and coordinated global policy action, rapid decarbonization across all sectors, and large-scale deployment of clean energy and negative-emission technologies.

The NZ2050 REMIND pathway ensures net-zero CO₂ emissions by midcentury, with residual non-CO₂ gases offset through negative-emission technologies such as bioenergy with carbon capture and sequestration (BECCS) and direct air capture (DAC). This results in 1.4°C of cumulative warming in 2100. Fossil fuel use declines by roughly 90% by mid-century, with unabated coal nearly eliminated by 2040 and sharp reductions in oil and gas. Global energy demand stabilizes as efficiency gains and electrification offset growth in activity.

NZ2050 represents the most ambitious pathway in the NGFS scenario set. NZ2050 builds on existing and announced policies but introduces stringent emissions limits and rapid technology innovation. Note that all NGFS scenarios are produced using three different Integrated Assessment Models (IAMs): REMIND-MAgPIE, MESSAGEix-GLOBIOM, and GCAM. These IAMs share the common assumptions that define each scenario, but may offer different projections based on underlying model structure. Technical users may wish to consult NGFS documentation to determine if a specific IAM best fits their applications.

coreDrivers.policies: Carbon price: the shadow carbon price reaches 183 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030 and 749 in 2050, the main lever moving investment and dispatch away from fossil fuels. Other: fossil-gas import restrictions constrain Europe's gas supply.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: Temperature and net-zero constraint: 1.5°C with global net zero CO2 around 2050, plus national net-zero targets (Table 37) met on time. REMIND applies the targets by its 12 regions (e.g. India as CO2-only).
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: REMIND optimises intertemporally over investment, O&M, fuel and emission costs, with adjustment costs on fast scale-up. Learning cuts solar PV from 866 to 318 US$2010/kW by 2050 here, so cost decline depends on deployment: wind and solar reach 85% of 2050 generation (Current Policies 72%). With carbon at 749 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, the cost ranking tilts further to low-carbon options.
coreDrivers.investmentChange: Low-carbon power investment moves from 0.99% of GDP (MER) in 2020 to 1.25% in 2050, an increase of 26%. Investment and GDP are solved jointly in REMIND's general equilibrium.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Shared SSP2 v3.0 population and GDP drive energy and material demand: 9.64 billion people in 2050 and GDP (MER) growing 2.15%/yr over 2020-2050. The assumptions are common to all NGFS scenarios; GDP differs from Current Policies only through transition costs (-3.56% in 2050).
coreDrivers.otherDrivers: Limited carbon dioxide removal: REMIND switches off direct air capture and enhanced weathering, forcing deeper gross cuts and higher carbon prices (749 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050; total CCS 4594 Mt CO2/yr). It is a technology-availability limit, not a cost, policy or target, so no other driver fits.

dependencies.dependency_description: Grid decarbonisation in Net Zero 2050 (REMIND) rests on the carbon price (183 US$2010/tCO2 in 2030, 749 in 2050). It lifts wind and solar from 10% of generation in 2020 to 85% in 2050 and cuts coal capacity to 1% of its 2020 level by 2040.

Power investment averages 2570 bn US$2010/yr over 2025-2050 (1.55x Current Policies), including 1135 bn/yr for grids, and must be financed. A 2050 carbon price of 749 US$2010/tCO2 erodes unabated fossil plant profitability.

With wind and solar at 85% of 2050 generation, grids, storage and flexibility must absorb variable output. REMIND prices batteries, hydrogen storage, grid expansion and curtailment as integration costs; storage reaches 8955 GW by 2050. Grid investment averages 1135 bn US$2010/yr (2025-2050). No hourly dispatch is reported, so curtailment cannot be checked.

Power CCS captures 142 Mt CO2/yr in 2050 (141 Mt from bioenergy), so the pathway needs CCS at commercial scale; CCS cost differences between models drive large gaps in fossil generation. Storage of 8955 GW in 2050 relies on continued storage cost declines (endogenous learning).

REMIND uses regional renewable potentials by grade (hydro capped near 50 EJ/yr) and MAgPIE biomass competing with food. Power BECCS reaches 141 Mt CO2/yr and primary biomass 92 EJ in 2050, so land limits the negative-emission part of the power transition. Wind and solar at 85% of 270 EJ draw on the regional potentials.

Steel decarbonisation in Net Zero 2050 (REMIND) is steered only through economy-wide carbon pricing (749 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050) and emissions constraints; no steel-specific industrial policy is described. Steel emissions change by -102% over 2020-2050.

At 749 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050, fossil ironmaking costs more, favouring electricity (11.6 EJ) and hydrogen (4.0 EJ) in steel in 2050. No steel investment or unit-cost data are reported, so financing needs cannot be quantified.

Hydrogen supplies 23% of steel final energy in 2050 in Net Zero 2050 (REMIND), so hydrogen production, transport and storage must reach steel sites. Economy-wide CO2 transport and storage investment is 25 bn US$2010/yr in 2050, none attributed to steel.

Hydrogen-based ironmaking must scale to 4.0 EJ (23% of steel energy) by 2050 in Net Zero 2050 (REMIND). It is not yet market-ready, and the documentation states no readiness or efficiency assumptions.

The only policy acting on aviation in Net Zero 2050 (REMIND) is the carbon price on transport fuel (749 US$2010/tCO2 in 2050); no aviation mandate such as SAF blending is represented. Passenger aviation goes from 6910 to 9350 bn pkm over 2020-2050.
Carbon-priced fuel holds 2050 passenger aviation to 51% of the Current Policies level (9350 vs 18312 bn pkm), so demand responds through price rather than fuel switching.
